reasoning: The only post to pass 10 reach was the 'What happens to your body in space' reel (24 reach, 79% skip, all non-followers). So I am reusing that body-centred 'what happens to your body' hook and the reel format, on a new evergreen topic with no news. This also runs the strategy's version B of the reel hook test: a direct claim with a shocking number on the first content slide (17 h awake = 0.05% blood alcohol). With 0 followers, a Trial Reel loses nothing and starts producing trial data. I chose palette 1 and mystery music because they matched the best performer. Five short slides keep the watch time tight. The caption question asks about personal experience to test whether that drives comments.
topic: Sleep deprivation effects on the body
hook: What happens to your body without sleep

slides.title: 17 hours awake
slides.body: After about 17 hours awake, your reaction speed and accuracy can match someone at 0.05% blood alcohol.
slides.image_prompt: Glowing digital alarm clock on a dark nightstand beside a half-empty glass, deep blue night light, moody cinematic atmosphere

slides.title: Microsleeps take over
slides.body: Your brain starts switching off for seconds at a time, even with your eyes open, often without you noticing.
slides.image_prompt: Empty highway at night with blurred headlights and fading lane lines, dreamlike motion blur, dark blue and amber tones

slides.title: Hunger hormones flip
slides.body: After two short nights, hunger hormone ghrelin rose 28% and fullness hormone leptin fell 18% in one study.
slides.image_prompt: Open fridge glowing in a dark kitchen at night, donuts and cake on the counter, cold blue light, cinematic mood

slides.title: Brain cleaning stops
slides.body: Sleep helps fluid wash waste out of the brain. In mice, the space between brain cells grew about 60% during sleep.
slides.image_prompt: Translucent glass brain model with glowing blue water flowing through it, dark background, soft scientific lighting

slides.title: The 264-hour record
slides.body: In 1964, a student stayed awake for 11 days. Guinness later stopped tracking the record because it is dangerous.
slides.image_prompt: Stack of torn calendar pages scattered beside a vintage alarm clock under a single desk lamp, dark room, warm and blue tones

cta: Follow so you never miss the next one
caption:
After about 17 hours awake, your brain can perform roughly like it does at 0.05% blood alcohol. Most people hit that point on a normal late night.

Skip sleep for longer and your hunger hormones shift, microsleeps creep in, and your brain's overnight cleaning shift gets cut short. Sources: Williamson & Feyer 2000, Spiegel et al. 2004, Xie et al. 2013 (Science).

What's the longest you've ever stayed awake?
